birthDate.help: The date of birth determines age, reference age and projection horizon. You can find it on official ID documents.

birthDate.errorMinAge: Date of birth must be at least 18 years ago.

propertyUsage.label: Usage

propertyValue.label: Estimated property value (CHF) - for assets
propertyValue.help: The market value is used for the net-asset calculation.

propertyMortgage.label: Mortgage (CHF)
propertyMortgage.help: The mortgage reduces net assets and affects expenses.

propertyLandArea.label: Plot area (m2)
propertyLandArea.help: The area provides context for the property.

bvg.intro: The following key figures feed directly into the pension calculation. Values can be adjusted manually if needed (e.g. without PDF import).
bvg.summaryHelp: This value feeds directly into the BVG projection. You can find it on your BVG pension fund certificate.
bvg.detailsNote: These detail fields mirror the figures from the BVG pension fund certificate (e.g. UBS). They can be pre-filled via PDF import or entered manually. The actual calculation primarily uses the key figures in the upper section.

asOfDate.label: Reference date
asOfDate.help: The reference date shows which certificate the data is from. It appears at the top of the pension certificate.

coordinationDeduction.label: Coordination deduction
coordinationDeduction.help: The coordination deduction affects the insured salary in the BVG. You can find it on the certificate or in the regulations.

insuredSalaryRentenplan.label: Insured salary pension plan
insuredSalaryRentenplan.help: This salary shows the insured part in the pension plan. Source is the detailed BVG pension fund certificate.

insuredSalaryBonusplan.label: Insured salary bonus plan
insuredSalaryBonusplan.help: This value captures the insured bonus part. It is shown as a separate plan on the pension certificate.

maxBuyinTotal.label: Max. buy-in total
maxBuyinTotal.help: The maximum buy-in shows possible tax-effective contributions. You can find it on the pension certificate.

maxBuyinRentenplan.label: Max. buy-in pension plan
maxBuyinRentenplan.help: This buy-in headroom applies to the pension-plan portion. The value appears on the detailed certificate.

maxBuyinBonusplan.label: Max. buy-in bonus plan
maxBuyinBonusplan.help: This value shows possible buy-ins in the bonus plan. It is documented in the fund regulations or pension certificate.

severance.intro: Enter or calculate the severance payment: choose between a fixed amount or a formula model.

amount.label: Severance amount (CHF)
amount.help: Total gross/net amount as the starting value for allocation and scenarios.

formulaModel.label: Calculation model
formulaModel.help: Choose the model for the manual severance calculation.
formulaModel.tenureSalaryDays: Tenure x salary x day factor

lastSalary.label: Last annual salary (CHF)
lastSalary.help: Base salary for all calculation models.

employmentStart.label: Employed from
employmentStart.help: Start date for calculating years of service.

employmentEnd.label: Employed until
employmentEnd.help: End date for calculating years of service.

dayFactor.label: Day factor
dayFactor.help: Factor per year of service (1-60), default 30.

monthFactor.label: Month factor
monthFactor.help: Number of monthly salaries per CO 339b (2-8).

maturity.label: Due date (month/year)
maturity.help: The due date controls the timing of tax and allocation calculations.

assets.cashIntro: Enter accounts and cash holdings per row. All values are normalised to CHF.
assets.investmentsIntro: Enter ETFs, stocks, savings plans and real-estate ETFs separately.

account.label: Account
account.help: Account name for clear identification. Use the name from your account or brokerage statement.

type.label: Type
type.help: The type categorises the assets for analyses. Choose per account kind.

amount.label: Amount
amount.help: The amount feeds into the CHF total. Value from the current account balance.

currency.label: Currency
currency.help: The currency drives the conversion to CHF for the overall view.

etf.label: ETF (CHF)
etf.help: ETF holdings show the liquid investment share. Source is your brokerage statement.

stocks.label: Stocks (CHF)
stocks.help: Stock values affect return and risk in scenarios. Based on your portfolio balance.

savings.label: Savings plans (CHF)
savings.help: Savings plans capture regular investments. Source is your plan in the bank or broker portal.

realEstate.label: Real-estate ETF (CHF)
realEstate.help: Real-estate ETFs are shown separately for the asset structure.

ahv.intro: Enter the AHV key figures. The expected AHV pension is calculated automatically and shown as a result.
ahv.importStructure: Import structure: year | annual income | total | age | AHV pension share

income.label: Estimated average annual income (CHF)
income.help: This income is the most important basis for the AHV estimate. Sources are your AHV statement, payslips or your contribution history.

plannedRetirementAge.label: Planned retirement age
plannedRetirementAge.help: Choose your planned retirement age between 58 and 70. The age is validated against your current profile age.

ahv.retirementAgeHint: The retirement age is between 58 and 70 and must be at least your profile age ({{minAge}}+).

contributionEstimate.label: Contribution estimate p.a. (CHF)
contributionEstimate.help: If a contribution history exists, the estimate is calculated automatically. Without history you can enter the value manually.

contributionYears.label: Contribution years (estimate)
contributionYears.help: Contribution years affect the entitlement to a full AHV pension. With gaps in the contribution record the pension is lower.

exactRetirementAge.label: Planned retirement age
exactRetirementAge.help: Sets the AHV start as in payout planning: at retirement, at the earliest 2 years before the reference age. Retiring earlier does not by itself reduce the AHV, because contributions continue until the reference age.

exactIncome.label: Estimated average annual income (CHF)
exactIncome.help: This value stays in sync as reference for exact and approximate calculation.

earlyYears.label: Early withdrawal (years before reference age)
earlyYears.help: Follows from the planned retirement age: AHV starts at retirement, at the earliest 2 years before the reference age. Each year of early withdrawal cuts the pension by 6.8 % for life.

lateYears.label: Deferral (years after reference age)
lateYears.help: Follows from the planned retirement age: retiring after the reference age defers the AHV (at most 5 years). Each year raises the pension by 5.2 %.

year.label: Year
year.help: The calendar year of the reported contribution data. You can find it on the IK statement.

income.label: Annual income
income.help: Relevant income for the respective year. Source is the AHV account statement or salary certificate.

total.label: Total
total.help: Sum of the relevant contributions in the year. Used for estimates.

age.label: Age
age.help: Age at year end, for chronological context of the contribution data.

rentShare.label: AHV pension share
rentShare.help: Optional share for internal traceability per year.

pillar3.intro: Payout-oriented planning for pillar 3a: accounts, duration, tax model and expected net payout value.

securities.label: Securities / ETFs / funds * (CHF)
securities.help: This amount shows your current 3a investment volume. You can find it on your brokerage or 3a account statement.

realEstateEquity.label: Real-estate equity (rental properties) (CHF)
realEstateEquity.help: Equity in rental properties is captured for the asset view. Sources are financing or tax documents.

accountCount.label: Number of pillar 3a accounts
accountCount.help: Multiple 3a accounts enable staggered withdrawals and lower progression. You can find the number in your 3a contracts.

accountBalance.label: Account {{index}} balance (CHF)
accountBalance.help: Balance per 3a account as basis for projection and tax planning. Value from the latest 3a statement.

accountReturn.label: Return (%)
accountReturn.help: Expected annual return for this account. Use conservative values per your investment strategy.

accountYears.label: Duration / years
accountYears.help: Number of years until withdrawal or retirement. This drives the compound-interest projection.

taxModel.label: Tax model (placeholder)
taxModel.help: The model controls how the capital-withdrawal tax is estimated. Cantonal tariffs apply for final values.

taxCanton.label: Canton (tax template)
taxCanton.help: The canton significantly affects the withdrawal tax. Use the expected canton of residence at withdrawal.

taxRate.label: Tax rate (%)
taxRate.help: This rate is used for the tax projection. If you know the target value you can override it manually.

monthlySavings.label: Monthly savings rate * (CHF)
monthlySavings.help: The monthly savings rate determines future 3a growth. Based on standing order or planned contributions.

baseReturn.label: Expected base return (%)
baseReturn.help: Base expectation for the projection of all 3a accounts. Align with your risk profile and long-term market expectations.

life.intro: Enter contract-based life insurance. Document import supports automatic extraction of capital and pension start from PDF policies.

insuranceType.label: Insurance type
insuranceType.help: This entry controls whether capital or annuity values are used for planning. You can find the type on your policy.

insurer.label: Insurer
insurer.help: The insurer helps assign policies and benefits. This information appears on the policy and premium invoice.

policyNumber.label: Policy number
policyNumber.help: The policy number uniquely identifies the policy.

currency.label: Currency
currency.help: Choose the calculation currency for the insurance.

capitalSum.label: Capital sum ({{currency}})
capitalSum.help: The capital sum shows the agreed benefit at maturity or event. You can find it on the policy under benefit/capital.

annualRent.label: Annual annuity payment ({{currency}})
annualRent.help: This value is used for the expected annual cash flow. Based on the annuity benefit shown on the policy.

entryAge.label: Entry age
entryAge.help: The entry age affects duration and assumptions. It appears at the contract start of your insurance.

surrenderValue.label: Surrender value ({{currency}})
surrenderValue.help: The surrender value is the amount upon early termination. It appears on statements or from the insurer.

monthlyPremium.label: Monthly premium ({{currency}})
monthlyPremium.help: Regular monthly premium from the policy.

sumAtDeath.label: Death benefit ({{currency}})
sumAtDeath.help: Benefit in case of death per the contract.

annualPremium.label: Annual premium ({{currency}})
annualPremium.help: The premium shows your regular annual expense. It appears on the premium invoice and policy.

maturityYear.label: Maturity year
maturityYear.help: The maturity year defines the benefit date in the plan. You can find it in your policy's contract data.

monthlyPension.label: Monthly pension at retirement ({{currency}})
monthlyPension.help: This payment flows into retirement planning as monthly income. Based on the guaranteed or expected annuity benefit.

capitalPayout.label: Capital benefit at maturity ({{currency}})
capitalPayout.help: This benefit is counted as a one-off payout. You can find the value on the policy under maturity benefit.

life.taxNote: Tax note: capital benefits are often taxed at a lower rate in Switzerland.

payoutPlan.title: Payout planning: pension or lump sum, staggering and investment
payoutPlan.intro: What changes if you take the pension fund as a pension or a lump sum, spread the 3a accounts over several years and take the life insurance (3b) as capital or a pension? Capital paid out is invested and drawn down so that it lasts until the target age.
payoutPlan.loading: Loading payout planning from the profile …
payoutPlan.kpiDraw: of which drawn from capital / month
payoutPlan.realNote: All amounts in today's purchasing power (inflation {{inflation}}% p.a.), before income tax on pensions and withdrawals.
payoutPlan.bvgCapitalHint: Value from the pension statement ("retirement assets at 65" or at the planned age). Pre-filled with today's assets.
payoutPlan.pillar3aHint: Each account is paid out in full in one year, from {{min}} at the earliest; after the reference age up to {{max}} only if still working. Payouts in the same year (including the pension fund lump sum) are taxed together.
payoutPlan.staggeringSaves: Staggering saves you {{amount}} in tax compared with paying out all accounts at {{age}}.
payoutPlan.staggeringHint: Tip: spread 3a payouts over different years, not in the year of the pension fund lump sum; that lowers the progression.
payoutPlan.lifeTaxNote: The lump sum of a surrenderable life insurance financed by periodic premiums is usually free of income tax at maturity (term of at least 5 years, signed before 66). A life annuity is partly taxable as income. Check the conditions of your own policy.
payoutPlan.variantNote: Monthly available = AHV + pensions + a constant draw from the invested capital so that it lasts until {{age}}. A pension is paid for life; capital can run out if you live long, but can be inherited if you die early.
payoutPlan.chartIncome: Monthly income by age (today's francs, pensions after estimated income tax)
payoutPlan.taxTable: Capital withdrawal tax per payout year
payoutPlan.taxSource: Source: ESTV tax calculator, tax year {{year}}, {{municipality}} ({{canton}}), without church tax. Interpolated between the official grid points.
payoutPlan.disclaimer: Simulation with the chosen assumptions, not investment or tax advice. Returns are not guaranteed; check your own pension fund's rules (lump sum, notice periods).
payoutPlan.kpiDrawOdds: lasts until {{age}} in {{percent}}% of market paths
payoutPlan.kpiSafeDrawHint: lasts until {{age}} in 9 of 10 simulated market paths
payoutPlan.bucketsSummary: Portfolio {{ret}}% p.a. after costs · volatility {{vol}}% · capital at retirement approx. {{amount}}
payoutPlan.bucketsHint: Capital paid out (pension fund, 3a, 3b, free assets) is split across the buckets by share and rebalanced yearly. Draws come proportionally from all buckets.
payoutPlan.bucketsAssumptions: Defaults are long-term assumptions (nominal, before costs), not forecasts: cash 0.5%, conservative 2.5%, balanced 3.5%, growth 4.5%, world equities 6%. Deliberately below the historical values of recent decades; all values editable.
payoutPlan.chartWealthBand: Line: plan at average return · dashed: median · area: 80% of simulated market paths (1000 paths)
payoutPlan.bvgAnnualCreditHint: How much capital is missing per year of earlier retirement (or added per year later). Pre-filled: 18% of the insured salary (BVG minimum from 55); adjust from your pension statement.
payoutPlan.partnerIncome: Partner's income in retirement (CHF net / month)
payoutPlan.partnerIncomeHint: For the comparison with the median of a retiree household; if empty only your income counts.
payoutPlan.medianTitle: Comparison with the median of retirees
payoutPlan.medianAbove: Retiring at {{age}}, your household has about {{net}} net per month from the start of AHV (with a safe draw). That is {{pct}} above the median of retirees ({{median}}). Without drawing down capital, i.e. pensions after tax only: {{pctNoDraw}}.
payoutPlan.medianBelow: Retiring at {{age}}, your household has about {{net}} net per month from the start of AHV (with a safe draw). That is {{pct}} below the median of retirees ({{median}}). Without drawing down capital, i.e. pensions after tax only: {{pctNoDraw}}.
payoutPlan.cmpNote: Net = AHV, fund and 3b pensions after estimated income tax ({{tax}}%) plus the draw from capital, in today's francs, excluding health insurance premiums (hence slightly too high). AHV from 63 at the earliest, reduced by 6.8% per year of early draw; conversion rate −5% per year earlier. Early retirees pay AHV contributions as non-earners until 65 (not deducted here).{{married}}
payoutPlan.cmpNoteMarried: Household = your income plus the partner's income entered; median of a couple = 1.5 × single person.
payoutPlan.medianSources: Median income: disposable income aged 65+, {{income}}; there is no finer breakdown by age above 65. Median wealth (dashed line in the wealth chart, up to 74): {{wealth}}, excluding pension fund and 3a — there is no Swiss-wide series by age.
payoutPlan.wealthOverviewTitle: Wealth overview to age 100: capital or pension
payoutPlan.wealthOverviewHint: The same payout plan (settings above) with 100 % pension-fund lump sum, with 100 % pension and with your choice. Invested wealth in today's francs, from retirement. With a pension less wealth remains, but income is higher.
payoutPlan.wealthOverviewMonthly: CHF {{amount}}/month from AHV start · capital tax CHF {{tax}}
payoutPlan.wealthOverviewEmpty: The overview appears once the payout plan is loaded.
payoutPlan.bvgBuyInIncluded: incl. buy-in from the severance with interest: {{amount}}
payoutPlan.buyInLock: Buy-in less than 3 years before the lump-sum withdrawal: the resulting benefits may not be taken as capital (BVG Art. 79b para. 3), otherwise the tax deduction is reversed. Choose a pension or withdraw later.
payoutPlan.profileChanged: The profile has different values than this plan (the plan keeps its own values): pension-fund capital {{bvg}}, 3b capital {{life}}, 3b pension {{lifePension}} p.a., 3a balances.
payoutPlan.lifeCurrency: The life insurance is recorded in {{currency}}; the plan treats the amounts as CHF without conversion. If needed, enter capital and pension here in CHF.
payoutPlan.sourcesTitle: Where the invested capital comes from
payoutPlan.sourcesHint: Each lump sum in the year it is paid out: gross, its share of the capital withdrawal tax (pension fund and 3a in the same year are taxed together, tax split by amount) and net. "Net today" in today's purchasing power; this total is split across the pots by their shares.
payoutPlan.src_buyIn: Buy-in from severance (in the pension fund)
payoutPlan.syncedTitle: Changed values taken over from the cards
payoutPlan.kpiSafeDrawNone: capital doesn't last in weak markets
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_monthly_good: Your net income is at or above the median of retirees your age.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_monthly_warn: Your net income is up to 15 % below the median of retirees your age.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_monthly_bad: Your net income is more than 15 % below the median of retirees your age.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_monthly_info: No median comparison is available for this household.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_draw_good: At least 9 in 10 simulated market paths sustain this draw until age {{age}}.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_draw_warn: 75–90 % of simulated market paths sustain the draw until age {{age}} – little buffer for weak market years.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_draw_bad: Fewer than 3 in 4 simulated market paths sustain the draw until age {{age}}. A lower draw or a later target age raises the odds.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_draw_info: The success rate is not simulated here.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_safe_good: The safe draw covers at least 90 % of the planned draw.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_safe_warn: The safe draw covers less than 90 % of the planned draw – the plan relies on average markets.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_safe_bad: In weak market paths the capital does not last until age {{age}}, even for a small draw.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_safe_info: The safe draw is not simulated here.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_tax_info: One-off tax on the lump sums (ESTV rates). Spreading withdrawals over several years often lowers it.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_wealth_good: At the target age of {{age}}, invested wealth remains as a reserve.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_wealth_info: The capital is used up as planned at {{age}} – no reserve for a longer life.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_portfolio_warn: Volatility {{vol}} % per year (above 12 %): in bad years wealth can fall noticeably.
payoutPlan.kpiWhy_portfolio_info: Expected return after costs; volatility of {{vol}} % per year is within the usual range.
payoutPlan.sched_hint: When each pot is paid out or its pension starts. Lump sums in the same year are taxed together and therefore progressively – spreading them saves tax.
payoutPlan.sched_bvgNote: Lump sum {{share}} %, rest as pension – from retirement
payoutPlan.sched_legend: Dot = lump sum, ring = pension start, gross amount in thousand CHF. Outline = payout year, red = several lump sums in the same year. Tax: lump-sum tax per year; bold = retirement.
payoutPlan.sched_clash: Several lump sums in the same year ({{years}}): they are added up and taxed at a higher rate. For tax reasons it makes sense to move the payout date of one pillar.
payoutPlan.sched_empty: No payouts from the 2nd pillar, 3a or 3b recorded.
